sentences.text: Gracilisuchus is an extinct genus of small pseudosuchians, a group of archosaurs that includes crocodile relatives, containing only one species, G. stipanicicorum.
This animal was tiny, with the largest known skull measuring slightly over 9 cm and a total body length estimated between 21 cm and 28 cm, weighing approximately 1.31 kg.
It was a small predator whose diet consisted mainly of insects and small vertebrates, protected by a double row of bony plates running from its spine to the tip of its tail.

Alfred Romer first described the genus and species Gracilisuchus stipanicicorum in 1972, based on a holotype discovered during a 1964–1965 expedition in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin of La Rioja Province, Argentina.
The holotype specimen is currently housed at the Museum of Paleontology at the National University of La Rioja with the catalog number PULR 08.

Romer initially classified Gracilisuchus as a relative of Ornithosuchus based on skull and skeletal similarities, but Cruickshank later removed it from Ornithosuchidae because it had a crocodile-normal ankle unlike other ornithosuchids.

Benton and Clark classified Gracilisuchus as a member of Suchia in 1988 based on a crocodile-normal ankle, while Sereno and Arcucci suggested in 1990 that ornithosuchids including Gracilisuchus were closer to crocodile-line archosaurs than dinosaurs.
It lived during the middle Triassic, specifically the Anisian and Ladinian stages, approximately 240 to 235 million years ago in what is now South America.
Its fossils were found in the Los Chañares Formation in La Rioja Province, in the Cuyo region of Argentina.

A vertebral series originally thought to belong to the tail of Gracilisuchus has been reassigned to the genus Tropidosuchus. It is debated whether a scapula and coracoid found overlapping the holotype belong to a second Gracilisuchus individual or are associated debris. Incomplete anatomical knowledge of Gracilisuchus hampered research until it was redescribed in papers published in 2011 and 2017. It is debated whether Ornithosuchus shares the close articulation between ischium halves seen in Gracilisuchus. Romer debated whether ornithosuchids were dinosaurs, citing basal archosaur traits like a closed acetabulum and osteoderms. Brinkman tentatively placed Gracilisuchus closer to crocodile-line archosaurs like Erythrosuchidae and Rauisuchidae than to Ornithosuchidae.
